who: Historian of modern France and the welfare state at Queen's University; PhD Columbia.

evidence.says: Queen's identifies Timothy Smith as a professor with a Columbia PhD, specializing in modern France, comparative public policy and the welfare state.
T. Lynn Smith is Thomas Lynn Smith, a sociology professor with a University of Minnesota PhD who taught at Louisiana State, Vanderbilt and Florida.
Timothy Lawrence Smith is the author of Revivalism and Social Reform.
The publisher's biography gives Timothy L. Smith a Harvard PhD in 1955 and appointments including Minnesota and Johns Hopkins.
This authority identifies Timothy B. Smith through This Great Battlefield of Shiloh, rather than the Queen's historian's works on France.
The publisher identifies the Civil War author Timothy B. Smith as a history teacher at the University of Tennessee at Martin.

notes: All three candidates are different people. In particular, p-71644's LC authority belongs to the Civil War historian, despite the compatible name.

who: John D. Turner, Nebraska professor of religious studies and historian of early Christianity; doctoral study at Duke.

evidence.says: Nispel's dissertation, posted on his own website, names Professor John Turner as supervisor at Nebraska and is dated December 2003.
Nebraska's account identifies Turner as its Cotner Professor since 1976, a specialist in Nag Hammadi texts who pursued his doctorate in early Christianity at Duke.
This John Turner is John Andrew Turner, lecturer in history at Bedford College, London, and author of Lloyd George's Secretariat.
John G. Turner earned his PhD at Notre Dame in 2006 and taught at South Alabama and George Mason, specializing in American history and religion.
The ORCID supplied for p-9424 identifies John Turner as a professor in the Business School at Queen's University Belfast.

notes: None of the supplied identifiers belongs to the Nebraska adviser. The ORCID contradicts p-9424's displayed name, John D. Turner. The supplied Columbia 1968 doctorate also conflicts with the adviser identified by the dissertation and Nebraska source.

who: Germán Vergara, environmental and Latin American historian at Georgia Tech; PhD history, Berkeley, 2015.

evidence.says: His institutional CV records a Berkeley history PhD in 2015 and Georgia Tech appointments beginning in 2017.
Georgia Tech identifies Vergara as an environmental and Latin American historian and author of Fueling Mexico: Energy and Environment, 1850–1950.
The candidate's LC authority cites Fueling Mexico and explicitly identifies its author Germán Vergara as a history professor at Georgia Tech.

notes: The LC record directly agrees on institution, field and work; the CV independently matches the supplied doctorate.

who: Pamela Voekel, historian of Mexico and Latin America, formerly at Georgia and now at Dartmouth; PhD Texas.

evidence.says: Georgia's graduate awards list records Derek Bentley as sponsored by Dr. Pamela Voekel in 2010, establishing her connection to the named student.
Dartmouth lists Voekel's University of Texas PhD, her Latin American history fields, and her books Alone Before God and For God and Liberty.
The LC authority identifies Pamela Voekel through Alone Before God and For God and Liberty, and explicitly names her Dartmouth history appointment.

notes: The candidate's works and Dartmouth affiliation match the institutional biography; Georgia independently connects her to Bentley.

who: Joel Thomas Walker, historian of late antiquity at the University of Washington; PhD history, Princeton, 1998.

evidence.says: Washington identifies Joel Thomas Walker as an associate professor specializing in late antiquity and early Christianity, with a Princeton history PhD in 1998.
The department describes graduate student Jeffrey Haines's work and quotes Professor Joel Walker about Haines's contribution.
J. Samuel Walker is identified as the historian of the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission and author of Three Mile Island.
J. R. Walker is James Riley Walker, author of The Sun Dance, published in 1917, and Lakota Society.
The remaining ORCID names Sam Walker and links a 2021 History of Education Quarterly review of Before March Madness.

notes: The supplied candidates identify J. Samuel/Sam Walker or James Riley Walker, not Joel Thomas Walker. Washington gives 1998 for his doctorate rather than the supplied 1997.

who: John Weiss, European historian at Wayne State in 1956–1968, later at Lehman College; PhD Columbia, 1958.

evidence.says: The biographical reference gives John Weiss a Columbia PhD in 1958 and Wayne State appointments from 1956 through 1968, matching the supplied degree and supervision period.
Herold Weiss earned a Duke PhD in 1964 and was a religious studies professor at Saint Mary's College, rather than the Columbia-trained Wayne State historian.
Holger Weiss earned his PhD at Helsinki in 1997, is a professor at Åbo Akademi, and has ORCID 0000-0002-8508-7613.
The ORCID confirms Holger Weiss's general history professorship at Åbo Akademi, beginning in 2003.
Hermann Weiss is the author/editor associated with Biographisches Lexikon zum Dritten Reich.
A scholarly article in this issue, printed page 95, identifies Hermann Weiß as an Institut für Zeitgeschichte employee from 1961 to 1997 and its longstanding deputy archive director.

notes: The matching Columbia degree and Wayne State period identify John Weiss. Herold, Holger (both candidate records) and Hermann Weiss have different degrees or institutional careers.

who: Kimberly Welch, Latin American cultural historian at St. John's University in 1994–2000, later Redlands; PhD UC San Diego.

evidence.says: Redlands identifies Welch as a Latin American cultural historian with a UC San Diego PhD and explicitly lists her St. John's history appointment in 1994–2000.
The candidate's LC authority identifies Kimberly M. Welch as author of Black Litigants in the Antebellum American South.
Vanderbilt identifies the author of that book as a historian of the United States, slavery and legal history, with a University of Maryland PhD in 2012.

notes: The St. John's supervisor and the Vanderbilt author are different historians: UC San Diego versus Maryland doctorates, and Latin American cultural history versus US legal history.

who: Winthrop Lindsay Adams, historian of ancient Greece and Rome at Utah since 1975; doctorate Virginia.

evidence.says: Utah identifies Winthrop Lindsay Adams as a history professor specializing in ancient Greece and Rome, appointed in 1975, with his doctorate from Virginia.
The candidate is William Mark (Bill) Adams, a Cambridge geographer specializing in conservation and development, associated with Nature's Place and Green Development.

notes: Winthrop Lindsay Adams at Utah is different from William Mark Adams at Cambridge.
